name: Fuse
author: E. T. Carter
description: The traveling fuse-spark mapped onto a circuit board: a lattice of faint copper traces and solder pads fills the frame, and white-hot charge pulses race along the rows and columns at their own speeds and directions, each ringed by a warm-to-cool halo, throwing spark flecks and dragging a glowing cooling trail that lights the traces behind it. The pulses light pads as they pass; staggered phases keep current flowing somewhere always.

params.label: Pulse speed
params.effect: How fast the charge pulses race along the traces.

params.label: Halo width
params.effect: Radius in CSS px of the colour-graded halo around each pulse head.

params.label: Spark spray
params.effect: Density of spark flecks thrown off each pulse head; 0 leaves clean ember points.

params.label: Trace density
params.effect: How fine the lattice is and how many edges are routed, from sparse traces to a packed board.

params.label: Pad glow
params.effect: Brightness of the copper traces and solder pads behind the pulses.
